dossier.purpose: Node.js/TypeScript server + CLI that crawls/ingests documentation (websites, GitHub repos, npm/PyPI pages, local folders and zip/tar archives; HTML, Markdown/MDX, PDF, Office, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, Jupyter, source code, JSON) into a local SQLite store as semantic chunks (FTS5 lexical index, optional sqlite-vec embeddings) and exposes search/list/version/fetch operations over MCP (stdio, SSE, Streamable HTTP), a yargs CLI and a React web UI (README.md:3,16-17; ARCHITECTURE.md:5-23). Facts for the stated needs: (1) Search = MCP tool `search_docs` and CLI `search`, both thin wrappers over `SearchTool`; hybrid FTS5 + vector (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) when an embedding provider is configured, FTS5-only otherwise; scoped per library[/version]; results are context-expanded chunk text plus source URL, not full original bodies, and the store keeps no source body (src/tools/SearchTool.ts:42-129; src/store/DocumentRetrieverService.ts:28-145; db/migrations/009-add-pages-table.sql:7-36). (2) The only body read-back is `fetch_url` (MCP) / `fetch-url` (CLI): a live re-fetch of an http(s) or file:// source converted to Markdown, without indexing (src/tools/FetchUrlTool.ts:47-146). No tool returns a stored page. (3) No standalone converter tool exists: document-to-Markdown conversion (PDF, docx/xlsx/pptx, doc/xls/ppt, ODF, RTF, EPUB, FB2, ipynb via @xberg-io/xberg; HTML via the HTML pipeline) is built into ingestion, and `fetch_url`/`fetch-url` exposes it one-shot as Markdown text (no JSON output). No OCR/scan option is configured or mentioned anywhere; image/video/audio/font types are skipped (src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.ts:105-109; src/utils/mimeTypeUtils.ts:390-430).

claims.claim: Fetches official docs from websites, GitHub, npm, PyPI and local files so the AI can query the exact version in use.
Private & Local: 'Runs entirely on your machine; your code never leaves your network.'
Multiple sources: index websites, GitHub repositories, local folders and zip archives.
Rich file support: HTML, Markdown, PDF, Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, Jupyter Notebooks and '90+ source code languages'.

Supported-formats table: Documents (PDF, .docx/.doc, .xlsx/.xls, .pptx/.ppt, .odt/.ods/.odp, RTF, EPUB, FictionBook, Jupyter), Archives (ZIP, TAR, tar.gz extracted and processed individually), Markup (Markdown, MDX, reStructuredText, AsciiDoc, Org Mode, Textile, R Markdown).
CLI first: `scrape <library> <url>` indexes, `search <library> 'query' --output yaml` queries, `fetch-url <url>` returns a single page as Markdown; requires Node.js 22+.
Structured commands default to JSON on stdout in non-interactive runs; --output json|yaml|toon; diagnostics kept off stdout; --quiet/--verbose.
Agent Skills in skills/ teach AI coding assistants to use the CLI (documentation search, index management, URL fetching).
MCP server: `npx @arabold/docs-mcp-server@latest`, web UI on http://localhost:6280, client config type sse with url http://localhost:6280/sse; `scrape_docs` accepts preserveHashes.
Docker alternative: ghcr.io/arabold/docs-mcp-server:latest with /data and /config volumes on port 6280.
Embedding model is optional but 'dramatically improves search quality by enabling semantic vector search'; OpenAI example, Ollama/Gemini/Azure and others documented.
Web scrapes probe llms.txt and send 'Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9, */*;q=0.8'; automatic, no configuration needed.
Search Quality Benchmark measures retrieval with IR metrics plus LLM-judged scores; Telemetry described as 'privacy-first usage data collection'.

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes — Docker image built for linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/release.yml:192); CI runs on ubuntu-latest with Node 22.x (.github/workflows/ci.yml:12,34,57,77); Xberg ships linux-x64 gnu and musl prebuilds (package-lock.json:5541-5572); Docker base is node:22-trixie-slim (Dockerfile:2) and the Linux gnu Xberg binary needs a recent glibc (GLIBC_2.38 error pinned in src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.test.ts:464-492; CHANGELOG.md:205).
platforms.wsl2: unknown — WSL/WSL2 is not mentioned in the README, docs or code (repo searched); it would take the Linux path but is neither documented nor CI-tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes — macOS paths are documented (docs/setup/configuration.md:9; docs/concepts/data-storage.md:202; .env.example:51), Xberg has a darwin-arm64 prebuild (package-lock.json:5493-5508) and the Docker image is built for arm64 ('Mac Silicon', release.yml:192); CI does not run on macOS (ci.yml uses ubuntu-latest only) and the lockfile lists no darwin-x64 Xberg prebuild (package-lock.json:5484-5491).
platforms.gpu: no — no GPU use or requirement anywhere in the repo; embeddings come from remote APIs or an external OpenAI-compatible server such as Ollama or LM Studio (docs/guides/embedding-models.md:59-79), which may use a GPU outside this project.

integrations.cli: yes — `docs-mcp-server` yargs CLI (package.json:6-8; src/cli/index.ts:168-180): default/server, mcp, web, worker, scrape, refresh, search, list, find-version, remove, fetch-url, compact, config. `search <library> <query> [--version X|range] [--limit 1-100, default 5] [--exact-match]` prints an array of {url, contentUrl, content, score, mimeType, sourceMimeType} as JSON (default), YAML or TOON (src/cli/commands/search.ts:13-109; src/cli/output.ts:19-43; src/store/types.ts:86-102). `fetch-url <url>` prints Markdown text only (src/cli/commands/fetchUrl.ts:14-81). Every invocation first runs the Playwright Chromium check (src/index.ts:16).
integrations.mcp: yes — stdio (src/mcp/startStdioServer.ts:14-28); SSE GET /sse + POST /messages and Streamable HTTP POST /mcp (stateless; GET returns 405) (src/services/mcpService.ts:54-196). Tools (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts): scrape_docs:97, refresh_version:206, search_docs:257, list_libraries:320, find_version:354, list_jobs:396, get_job_info:441, cancel_job:474, remove_docs:504, fetch_url:542; resources docs://libraries, docs://libraries/{library}/versions, docs://jobs, docs://jobs/{jobId} (:577-722). `search_docs` takes library, version (exact or X-range), query, limit (default 5), always uses non-exact version matching and returns plain text blocks 'Result N: <url>' + content without score or mime type (:257-316). No tool or resource returns a stored page or original body. `--read-only` (or DOCS_MCP_READ_ONLY) removes scrape_docs, refresh_version, list_jobs, get_job_info, cancel_job, remove_docs and the job resources (:95,394,621). Optional OAuth2/OIDC on /mcp and /sse (docs/infrastructure/authentication.md:5-19). Smithery install is documented (docs/guides/mcp-clients.md:284-289).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No SDK or library entry: package.json declares `bin` only, no main/exports/types (package.json:1-22). HTTP API: tRPC (superjson) router at /api over HTTP plus WebSocket subscriptions, enabled in the default unified command and in worker mode but not in `mcp` HTTP mode (src/services/trpcService.ts:28-82; src/cli/commands/default.ts:186-191; src/cli/commands/mcp.ts:199-205). Procedures include search, listLibraries, removeVersion, removeAllDocuments, compact, listVersionChunks (stored chunks, used by the admin UI), enqueueScrapeJob, getJobs (src/store/trpc/router.ts:40-355; src/pipeline/trpc/router.ts:67-153). Documented as internal worker/coordinator and web-UI plumbing and not protected by OAuth (docs/infrastructure/authentication.md:11); no OpenAPI/REST reference found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: yes — `claude mcp add docs-mcp-server -- npx -y @arabold/docs-mcp-server@latest` (docs/guides/mcp-clients.md:184-191) plus Agent Skills docs-search, docs-manage and fetch-url under skills/ (skills/docs-search/SKILL.md; docs/setup/installation.md:127-133; docs/guides/basic-usage.md:106-122); skills are not in the npm `files` list (package.json:15-22), so they must be copied from GitHub. Codex: none found (no Codex mention in docs or code). The .claude/, .agents/, .github/prompts and openspec/ files are the maintainers' own OpenSpec development workflow, not an integration.

readme.telemetry_and_network: TELEMETRY: on by default (src/utils/config.ts:81; src/telemetry/TelemetryConfig.ts:13). Events (app_started/shutdown, cli_command, tool_used, pipeline_job_*, captured exceptions with stack traces) go to PostHog at https://app.posthog.com via posthog-node (src/telemetry/postHogClient.ts:92,121-126; src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:18-26) only when the build embedded a key (vite.config.ts:29; telemetry.ts:45,54-55). The release workflow injects secrets.POSTHOG_API_KEY into the npm build and the Docker build (.github/workflows/release.yml:73-74,193-194; Dockerfile:17-19), so published artifacts can transmit; a source build without the variable sends nothing (.env.example:11-14). A persistent UUID in <store>/installation.id is the distinct id (TelemetryConfig.ts:41-70); geoip disabled (postHogClient.ts:99). Opt-out: --no-telemetry (src/cli/index.ts:63-71), DOCS_MCP_TELEMETRY=false (src/utils/config.ts:444), app.telemetryEnabled: false (docs/infrastructure/telemetry.md:271-281). Docs say no URLs, document content or search queries are collected (telemetry.md:9) but code sends the full search query from the CLI (src/cli/commands/search.ts:69-77), full URLs from CLI scrape/fetch-url (scrape.ts:165-181; fetchUrl.ts:50-56), the first 100 characters of the query from MCP search_docs (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:281-288), library names, and unsanitized job error messages (src/telemetry/TelemetryService.ts:80-90); the sanitizer helpers are never called outside tests (src/telemetry/sanitizer.ts). OTHER NETWORK: crawling targets over HTTP or Playwright, with private/loopback ranges blocked by default and a file-access allowlist defaulting to $DOCUMENTS (docs/infrastructure/security.md:30-43,76-78; src/utils/config.ts:126-139); GitHub API (src/scraper/strategies/GitHubScraperStrategy.ts:382,428) with optional GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token` (src/scraper/strategies/github-auth.ts:12-14,54); npm/PyPI strategies (src/scraper/ScraperRegistry.ts:41-49); embedding providers: OpenAI by default model name, or Vertex, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint via OPENAI_API_BASE (src/store/embeddings/EmbeddingFactory.ts:113-276) — optional: without credentials the store logs a warning and runs FTS5-only (src/store/DocumentStore.ts:688-697), while with credentials every query is also sent to the provider (:2340-2343). Each CLI/MCP start runs `npm exec -y playwright install --no-shell --with-deps chromium` if no Chromium is found (src/cli/utils.ts:64-105; src/index.ts:16); PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 skips it. dotenv loads a .env from the working directory (src/index.ts:4). The web UI in the browser calls api.github.com for an update check (src/web/client/hooks/useUpdateCheck.ts:11-12) and tries https://{host}/favicon.ico per library (src/web/client/components/LibIcon.tsx:57). No account or hosted service is required to run it.

languages: TypeScript (server, CLI, React TSX web client)

entry_points.what: Process entry, built to dist/index.js and exposed as bin `docs-mcp-server` (package.json:6-8): loads dotenv, normalizes env vars, calls ensurePlaywrightBrowsersInstalled(), then runCli() (src/index.ts:4-22).

yargs program with global flags (--output, --quiet, --verbose, --store-path, --config, --no-telemetry) and command registration (src/cli/index.ts:46-180); SIGINT and cleanup handling in main.ts:30-113.
`$0` / `server`: unified mode — stdio MCP when no TTY, otherwise Fastify HTTP with MCP (/mcp, /sse), tRPC /api, embedded worker and web UI on :6280 (default.ts:93-213).
MCP-only server over stdio or HTTP (web UI and /api disabled), optional --server-url external worker, --read-only, OAuth flags (mcp.ts:94-231).

createMcpServerInstance registers the 10 MCP tools and 4 resources (mcpServer.ts:74-726); tool wiring in src/mcp/tools.ts:47-67; HTTP/SSE routes in src/services/mcpService.ts:31-218; stdio in src/mcp/startStdioServer.ts.
CLI wrappers over SearchTool, ScrapeTool and FetchUrlTool in src/tools/ (same business logic the MCP tools call).
Distributed mode: worker (pipeline + store + /api on :8080) and web coordinator using --server-url (docs/infrastructure/deployment-modes.md:32-52; docker-compose.yml:8-114).

code.architecture: Layered: interfaces (src/cli; src/mcp + src/services/mcpService.ts; React SPA in src/web/client served by src/app/AppServer.ts) -> shared business logic in src/tools (SearchTool, ScrapeTool, FetchUrlTool, RefreshVersionTool, RemoveTool, job tools) -> pipeline (src/pipeline: PipelineManager/Worker/Client, persisted job state; src/events EventBus; tRPC in src/services/trpcService.ts) -> scraper (src/scraper: strategies Web/LocalFile/GitHub/Npm/PyPi; fetchers Http/Browser(Playwright)/File/AutoDetect; content pipelines in src/scraper/pipelines in order Json, SourceCode, Document (@xberg-io/xberg -> Markdown), Html, Markdown, Text; include/exclude, scope and access-policy utilities) -> splitter (src/splitter: SemanticMarkdownSplitter + GreedySplitter, JSON/text/tree-sitter splitters) -> store (src/store: DocumentStore on better-sqlite3 with FTS5 `documents_fts` and sqlite-vec `documents_vec`; DocumentRetrieverService + assembly strategies; LangChain embedding providers in src/store/embeddings; 17 SQL migrations in db/migrations). Cross-cutting: Zod config loader src/utils/config.ts (defaults < config.yaml < env < CLI), OAuth2/JWT proxy src/auth, PostHog telemetry src/telemetry. Search path: SearchTool -> DocumentManagementService.searchStore (src/store/DocumentManagementService.ts:697-705) -> DocumentRetrieverService.search -> DocumentStore.findByContent: FTS5 (porter unicode61; bm25 weights 10/1/5/1 over content/title/url/path; query = exact phrase OR any term) plus sqlite-vec KNN when embeddings are active, fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60, weights 1/1, FTS overfetch x2, vector x10), no lexical-only/vector-only switch (src/store/DocumentStore.ts:212-257,988-993,2312-2487; db/migrations/009-add-pages-table.sql:97-103; src/utils/config.ts:163-168). Hits are grouped per URL, clustered by sort_order distance <= 3, expanded with parent, 1 preceding sibling, 3 children and 2 subsequent siblings, and joined with blank lines (src/store/DocumentRetrieverService.ts:28-193; src/store/assembly/strategies/MarkdownAssemblyStrategy.ts:54-148; src/utils/config.ts:172-178). Chunk metadata holds only level/path/types, so results carry URL and mime types but no page numbers or offsets (src/store/types.ts:32-40,86-102). reStructuredText, AsciiDoc, Org and Textile are indexed as source-code text, not converted to Markdown (docs/concepts/supported-formats.md:165-178).
code.packaging_and_release: npm package @arabold/docs-mcp-server v3.2.1 (tag f2938c4, CHANGELOG.md:1; .git/packed-refs:2), bin docs-mcp-server -> dist/index.js, files: dist, public, db, README.md, LICENSE, package.json (package.json:6-22), built with Vite (package.json:25; vite.config.ts:9-74). Release workflow .github/workflows/release.yml is workflow_dispatch only (:3-9) and does not run lint or tests: npm ci, build with POSTHOG_API_KEY and APP_VERSION (:71-76), semantic-release (commit-analyzer, notes, changelog, npm publish, git commit of package.json/CHANGELOG, GitHub release with no assets: .releaserc.json:1-35) using the NPM_TOKEN secret, or a manual `npm publish --access public` path (:86-93). `id-token: write` is commented out (:20), so no npm provenance is configured. docker_publish job builds multi-arch linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 and pushes ghcr.io/arabold/docs-mcp-server tags (version, major.minor, major, latest) (:130-194) plus a GitHub build-provenance attestation pushed to the registry (actions/attest-build-provenance@v4, :196-201). No checksums, cosign signatures, standalone binaries or release assets found; actions are pinned by tag, not commit SHA. Dockerfile runs as non-root `node` with /app root-owned and /data,/config volumes (Dockerfile:64-90).
code.tests_and_ci: Vitest (vite.config.ts:75-101; package.json:33-43) with MSW, nock and memfs mocks. About 146 test files: 124 unit tests under src/ (*.test.ts), 20 e2e files under test/ (incl. mcp-stdio, mcp-http, cli, vector-search, local-file-pdf, docker-e2e; *-live-e2e excluded by default), 2 under tests/search-eval; roughly 2,700 describe/it/test calls (grep count). Real fixtures for pdf/docx/xlsx/pptx/ipynb in test/fixtures; Xberg is partly mocked in DocumentPipeline.test.ts:16. CI .github/workflows/ci.yml (push/PR to main, ubuntu-latest, Node 22.x only): lint (biome + tsc typecheck), test (installs Playwright Chromium, `npm test`), build, docker-test (builds image, runs test:docker incl. Xberg PDF extraction). .github/workflows/eval.yml: weekly (Mon 07:00 UTC) + manual search benchmark needing OpenAI/Anthropic/Google keys, not PR-gating. No macOS/Windows/WSL CI, no CodeQL/dependabot/renovate found. Husky pre-commit runs lint-staged (.husky/pre-commit:1); commits enforced by commitlint (CONTRIBUTING.md:41-53).
code.dependencies: package.json: 63 direct dependencies (:51-115) and 37 devDependencies (:116-154); package-lock.json (npm). engines node >=22 (:155-157); overrides npm 10.9.3 (:158-160). Notable: better-sqlite3 and sqlite-vec (native), tree-sitter + js/python/ts grammars (native), @xberg-io/xberg ~1.0.14 (MIT; optional native prebuilds darwin-arm64, linux arm64/x64 gnu+musl, win32-x64: package-lock.json:5476-5588), playwright, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0, langchain + @langchain/{openai,aws,google-genai,google-vertexai,core,textsplitters}, fastify 5, @trpc/*, react 19 + react-router + tanstack query, cheerio, jsdom, linkedom, turndown, remark/unified, defuddle, posthog-node, jose, zod 4, yargs 18, axios. Dockerfile notes npm 10 installs both glibc and musl native builds (~190 MB, over half Xberg) and prunes the musl ones (Dockerfile:27-33).
code.security_policy: none — no SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS, dependabot or renovate config found; docs/infrastructure/security.md is a deployment-hardening guide (trust boundaries, outbound network and file-access policy), not a vulnerability-reporting policy.

claim_checks.claim: Private & Local: runs entirely on your machine; your code never leaves your network (README.md:14)
claim_checks.evidence: Indexing/search storage is local SQLite (src/store/DocumentStore.ts:259-280), but telemetry defaults on (src/utils/config.ts:81; src/telemetry/TelemetryConfig.ts:13) and posts to https://app.posthog.com (src/telemetry/postHogClient.ts:92) in builds that embed a key, which the release workflow injects (.github/workflows/release.yml:73-74,193-194; vite.config.ts:29). The default embedding model text-embedding-3-small uses OpenAI whenever OPENAI_API_KEY is present, sending chunk text at index time and the query at every search (src/utils/config.ts:83; src/store/embeddings/EmbeddingFactory.ts:136-163; src/store/DocumentStore.ts:2340-2343). Crawling fetches remote sites, and the web UI browser calls api.github.com (src/web/client/hooks/useUpdateCheck.ts:11-12). Fully local use needs telemetry opted out and FTS-only or a local OpenAI-compatible embedder.

claim_checks.claim: Rich File Support: PDF, Word/Excel/PowerPoint, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, Jupyter and '90+ source code languages' (README.md:17)
claim_checks.evidence: Document formats confirmed: isSupportedDocument covers PDF, docx/xlsx/pptx, doc/xls/ppt, odt/ods/odp, RTF, EPUB, FB2, ipynb (src/utils/mimeTypeUtils.ts:390-400); DocumentPipeline calls Xberg extract() with Markdown output (src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.ts:105-109) and is in the standard pipeline list (src/scraper/pipelines/PipelineFactory.ts:32-41). The '90+' figure is not supported: the language map has 77 distinct ids including markup/config/data formats (src/utils/mimeTypeUtils.ts:495-632) and the docs list about 74 (docs/concepts/supported-formats.md:103-207). Scanned or image-only inputs: no OCR option is passed or mentioned anywhere; image/video/audio/font types are skipped (src/utils/mimeTypeUtils.ts:421-430; src/scraper/strategies/LocalFileStrategy.ts:19-23,333-337).

claim_checks.claim: Using an embedding model is optional but dramatically improves search quality (README.md:125)
claim_checks.evidence: Optional is confirmed: with no credentials the store warns and runs FTS5-only (src/store/DocumentStore.ts:688-697; FTS-only branch :2443-2487); with credentials it runs hybrid vector + FTS with RRF (:2340-2442; :212-221). 'Dramatically' is not measured: the only checked-in benchmark was recorded with text-embedding-3-small (tests/search-eval/baseline.json:5) and there is no FTS-only baseline. Hybrid always includes FTS; search has no vector-only or lexical-only switch (src/tools/SearchTool.ts:7-13).

claim_checks.claim: Fetch a single page as Markdown with fetch-url (README.md:61-65)
claim_checks.evidence: src/cli/commands/fetchUrl.ts:14-81 and MCP fetch_url (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:542-575) call FetchUrlTool, which fetches http(s) or file:// (file access subject to the policy: src/scraper/fetcher/FileFetcher.ts:18-38), runs the standard pipelines including DocumentPipeline for PDF/Office/EPUB, and returns textContent without indexing (src/tools/FetchUrlTool.ts:47-146). Markdown sources pass through unchanged (src/scraper/pipelines/MarkdownPipeline.ts:77-84). Output is Markdown text only, never JSON; the 10 MB document cap applies (src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.ts:72-85).

SSE route src/services/mcpService.ts:54-127, Streamable HTTP /mcp :153-196, stdio src/mcp/startStdioServer.ts:14-28; default bind host 127.0.0.1 and port 6280 (src/utils/config.ts:87-93; AppServer listen at src/app/AppServer.ts:153-156). The standalone `mcp` command serves MCP only, without web UI or /api (src/cli/commands/mcp.ts:199-205).

claim_checks.claim: Telemetry is privacy-first and 'Never collects URLs, document content, search queries, or authentication tokens' (README.md:162 -> docs/infrastructure/telemetry.md:9)
claim_checks.evidence: CLI `search` sends the full query (src/cli/commands/search.ts:69-77); CLI `scrape` and `fetch-url` send the full url (src/cli/commands/scrape.ts:165-181; src/cli/commands/fetchUrl.ts:50-56); MCP search_docs sends the first 100 characters of the query plus library/version (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:281-288); job failures send job.error.message unsanitized (src/telemetry/TelemetryService.ts:80-90). The sanitizer helpers (extractHostname, analyzeSearchQuery, sanitizeErrorMessage) have no non-test call sites (src/telemetry/sanitizer.ts). Opt-out exists: --no-telemetry, DOCS_MCP_TELEMETRY=false (src/cli/index.ts:63-71; src/utils/config.ts:444). Code wins over the doc.

claim_checks.claim: Read-only mode 'Prevent modification of data (scraping/indexing)' (docs/setup/configuration.md:159; CLI help src/cli/commands/default.ts:67-73)
claim_checks.evidence: Enforced only by not registering MCP write/job tools and job resources (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:95,394,621); config.app.readOnly is otherwise only surfaced as a status display (src/services/systemInfo.ts:82). The tRPC /api enabled in the default and worker modes has no read-only or auth check and exposes enqueueScrapeJob and removeAllDocuments (src/services/trpcService.ts:36-49; src/pipeline/trpc/router.ts:69-89; src/store/trpc/router.ts:121-135). CLI scrape/remove operate directly on the local store.

claim_checks.claim: MCP and CLI tools keep identical interfaces (ARCHITECTURE.md:320)
claim_checks.evidence: Both call the same SearchTool (src/tools/SearchTool.ts:42-129) but the surfaces differ: CLI search has --exact-match, --embedding-model, --server-url and emits structured results with score, mimeType, sourceMimeType, contentUrl (src/cli/commands/search.ts:30-58,109; src/store/types.ts:86-102); MCP search_docs fixes exactMatch=false and returns plain text blocks without score/mime/contentUrl (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:290-312). CLI scrape/fetch-url accept --header, --scrape-mode, --clean, --max-concurrency that MCP scrape_docs and fetch_url do not expose (src/cli/commands/scrape.ts:51-129; src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:97-140,542-552).

claim_checks.claim: Reference benchmark table comparing default Cheerio, Defuddle and Context7 (docs/guides/benchmarking.md:332-393)
claim_checks.evidence: The Cheerio column matches the checked-in baseline (MRR 0.747, Hit@5 0.881: tests/search-eval/baseline.json:36-46, recorded 2026-05-19). The Context7 column (MRR 0.733) is stale: tests/search-eval/baseline.context7.json, recorded 2026-09-20, has MRR 0.695 and Hit@1 0.559 and lists regressions against the earlier 0.733 baseline (baseline.context7.json:2,36-46,104-168). risks: Privacy/egress differs from README.md:14: telemetry is on by default (src/utils/config.ts:81) and release builds receive a PostHog key (.github/workflows/release.yml:73-74,193-194); the CLI sends raw search queries and URLs (src/cli/commands/search.ts:69-77; scrape.ts:165-181), contradicting docs/infrastructure/telemetry.md:9, and the sanitizer helpers are unused (src/telemetry/sanitizer.ts). An OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment or a .env in the working directory (loaded at src/index.ts:4) silently activates OpenAI embeddings of all chunks and every query (src/utils/config.ts:83; src/store/DocumentStore.ts:2340-2343), and there is no query-time FTS fallback if the embedding call fails (src/store/DocumentStore.ts:2488-2493).

No index-backed original-body read-back: the store keeps chunks and page metadata only (db/migrations/009-add-pages-table.sql:7-36). Markdown is re-serialized via remark -> HTML -> Turndown, frontmatter becomes its own chunk, horizontal rules are dropped and heading anchors stripped (src/splitter/SemanticMarkdownSplitter.ts:19-43,137-199,360-362), so chunk text is not byte-identical to the source; results are context-expanded groups (src/store/DocumentRetrieverService.ts:101-145), carry no page numbers or offsets (src/store/types.ts:32-40,86-102), and MCP output omits score/mime/contentUrl (src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:299-312). The only read-back is a live `fetch_url` of the source (it may differ from what was indexed or be gone; limited by the file/network policy) or the unauthenticated tRPC listVersionChunks (src/store/trpc/router.ts:274).

Exposure and auth: OAuth2 covers only /mcp and /sse, and POST /messages has no auth preHandler (src/services/mcpService.ts:129-151); the tRPC /api (search, enqueueScrapeJob, removeAllDocuments, compact) is unauthenticated by design (docs/infrastructure/authentication.md:11; src/services/trpcService.ts:36-49) and is on in the default command (src/cli/commands/default.ts:186-191); --read-only only hides MCP write tools. The README Docker command, Dockerfile and compose bind 0.0.0.0 and publish ports (README.md:113-119; Dockerfile:80-81; docker-compose.yml:15-19,59-60,94-95). No Origin/Host validation or CORS handling found in src/app, src/services or src/mcp (grep). `fetch_url` lets an MCP client trigger outbound requests and read files under the allowed roots, default $DOCUMENTS (src/tools/FetchUrlTool.ts:40-46; docs/infrastructure/security.md:76-78).

Startup side effect: every CLI or MCP start may run `npm exec -y playwright install --no-shell --with-deps chromium` (network download; Playwright's --with-deps installs OS packages, which on Linux normally needs elevated rights) and calls process.exit(1) if that fails, even for read-only `search`/`list` (src/index.ts:16; src/cli/utils.ts:64-105). The README does not mention it; offline or sandboxed hosts must set PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 or a Chromium path. A first-run download could also delay an MCP client's stdio startup (inference).

Ingestion controls that silently drop content: default exclude patterns (CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE*, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, *.test.*, **/archive|old|legacy|test|tests|spec|build|dist|out/**, *.conf/ini/cfg/log, i18n locales) apply unless the caller passes its own excludes (src/scraper/utils/defaultPatterns.ts:11-140); for file:// URLs they are matched against the absolute pathname, so a collection under an ancestor directory with such a name would match (inferred from src/scraper/utils/patternMatcher.ts:146-185; not run). Defaults maxDepth 3 and maxPages 1000 also bound local directory trees, where each directory level counts as depth (src/utils/config.ts:103-104; src/scraper/strategies/BaseScraperStrategy.ts:639-640; inferred), and file access allows only $DOCUMENTS, which resolves to nothing on hosts without ~/Documents (docs/setup/configuration.md:241-262). Re-scraping defaults to clean=true, replacing the version's content (src/cli/commands/scrape.ts:125-129).

Document conversion rests on @xberg-io/xberg ~1.0.14 prebuilt native binaries (extraction was switched from Kreuzberg to Xberg in v2.5.0: CHANGELOG.md:96,205); glibc-sensitive on Linux (GLIBC_2.38 error pinned in src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.test.ts:464-492), no darwin-x64 build (package-lock.json:5484-5491), 10 MB default size cap (src/utils/config.ts:124). Nothing in the repo configures or tests OCR, scanned PDFs or complex layouts: fixtures are small samples and Xberg is partly mocked in unit tests (src/scraper/pipelines/DocumentPipeline.test.ts:16; test/fixtures/), and no conversion-quality benchmark exists.

Platform/runtime constraints: Node 22 in practice because better-sqlite3 ships a Node-ABI-pinned binary (AGENTS.md:38; docs/guides/benchmarking.md:101-104); CI runs only on ubuntu-latest with Node 22 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:12,34,57,77); WSL2 is undocumented and macOS is not CI-tested; native modules (better-sqlite3, sqlite-vec, tree-sitter, Xberg) must be installable on the host, and the Docker image needs Chromium from apt (Dockerfile:45-52).

Maintenance and provenance: CONTRIBUTING.md:16 says most code was generated by an AI assistant; docs drift from code (ARCHITECTURE.md:29,305-309 still describe an HTMX/Alpine UI and line 44 links a missing docs/concepts/configuration.md; docs/setup/configuration.md:199 gives fetcher.maxRetries 6 vs 3 in src/utils/config.ts:113; docs/infrastructure/deployment-modes.md:93-97 says the standalone server recovers jobs by default but --resume defaults false at src/cli/commands/default.ts:62-66,162; the MCP server reports a hard-coded version 0.1.0 at src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:81-82). CHANGELOG has no v3.0.0 entry (CHANGELOG.md:77-84) amid fast releases (v2.5.0 on 2026-08-06 to v3.2.1 on 2026-09-27); 3.2.0 changed index text normalization and version-label handling (CHANGELOG.md:35-47). No SECURITY.md, npm provenance or artifact signatures (release.yml:20); the only benchmarks are self-run on a draft 59-query web-docs dataset with an LLM judge.
